articles.title: Veja motivos que fazem conta de luz no Brasil ser mais cara do que a de outros países com o mesmo perfil de geração de energia | G1
articles.standfirst: Um estudo encomendado pelo Centro de Liderança Pública mostra que mais de dois terços da fatura não têm relação com o custo da energia em si.
articles.summary: Um estudo encomendado pelo Centro de Liderança Pública mostra que mais de dois terços da fatura não têm relação com o custo da energia em si.
articles.body:
Um estudo listou os motivos que fazem a conta de luz no Brasil ser mais cara do que a de outros países com o mesmo perfil de geração de energia.

Uma mini cidade na Zona Norte do Rio com mais de 400 apartamentos e 3 mil moradores. A estrutura é moderna, com tomadas, lâmpadas e elevadores inteligentes. Mas a conta de luz chega a R$ 40 mil por mês e é um dos itens que mais sobrecarregam o preço do condomínio.

“Ela vai refletir aí entre 20% até 40% do custo total do boleto. Isso nos impede de fazer novos investimentos”, afirma o síndico profissional Jorge Lima.

Veja motivos que fazem conta de luz no Brasil ser mais cara do que a de outros países com o mesmo perfil de geração de energia — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Entre os produtos e serviços que compõem o índice de inflação, a energia tem o terceiro maior peso. Só perde para a gasolina e planos de saúde. Mas por que, se quase 90% da nossa energia vem de fontes renováveis, principalmente das usinas hidrelétricas e com participação crescente da eólica e solar?

Um estudo do economista da Fundação Getúlio Vargas Daniel Duque, encomendado pelo Centro de Liderança Pública, mostra que mais de dois terços da fatura não têm relação com o custo da energia em si. Em 2025, a parcela referente à energia respondia por cerca de 30,4% da conta de luz. Ou seja, em uma conta de R$ 1 mil, apenas R$ 300 correspondem à energia elétrica. A distribuição, 26%; transmissão, 10%; encargos setoriais que mantêm programas sociais e subsídios, por exemplo, para a irrigação na agricultura: 15%; e tributos, 18%.

A exigência de leis que determinam a compra de parte da energia de termelétricas e hidrelétricas de pequeno porte e o sistema de bandeiras tarifárias, que encarece a luz quando a seca reduz a água nas hidrelétricas, também contam.

Em um ranking de 138 países, o Brasil não está no topo com energia mais cara. Mas temos tarifa acima de países com o mesmo perfil renovável, como Canadá, Noruega e China, que conseguem converter o uso desses recursos em preços mais baixos.

“A gente também precisaria de uma maior coordenação, por exemplo, entre governo federal, estadual e municipais para, por exemplo, reduzir as perdas de transmissão e distribuição, que também são mais altas no Brasil do que em outros lugares do mundo”, afirma Daniel Duque, economista da FGV Ibre.

“Olha, eu estou agora em uma grande empresa de processamento de pescado. Sabe a temperatura aqui? - 25ºC na câmara fria. É claro que o preço da energia elétrica pesa, e muito, no orçamento do setor produtivo. A indústria passa a ter produtos mais caros e perde competitividade com outros países. Aqui nessa indústria, a energia é fundamental durante todo o processo, do barco do pescador até a mesa do consumidor final”, diz o repórter Helter Duarte.

A empresa existe há 82 anos e o custo da energia elétrica é um entrave cada vez maior para o crescimento. Para reduzir os custos, a fábrica investiu pesado em produção de energia solar, com duas usinas; trocou equipamentos por outros mais eficientes; e usa a inteligência artificial para gerir o consumo. A redução no custo chega a 30%.

“O cenário ideal seria uma política pública que trouxesse essa energia que a gente produz com bastante eficiência, uma energia limpa, barata. Teria como consequência produtos mais baratos na mesa do consumidor, mais emprego, mais investimento, mais trabalho e renda, e, consequentemente, um crescimento maior do nosso país”, afirma Cacio de Moura Rodrigues, gerente de Meio Ambiente da Frescatto.

articles.title: Powerful Haitian gang leader tells AP he wrote UN seeking dialogue as clashes intensify
articles.summary: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) — One of Haiti’s most powerful gang leaders confirmed to The Associated Press on Monday that he wrote the U. Secretary General and...
articles.body:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) — One of Haiti's most powerful gang leaders confirmed to The Associated Press on Monday that he wrote the U.N. Secretary General and requested that the organization send a delegation to Haiti for dialogue and mediation amid fears that Salvadoran troops deployed after the disappearance of four aviation technicians from that country could escalate violence.

Wilson Joseph, best known as Lanmò Sanjou and leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, told the AP in his first interview with a major international media company that the technicians are dead and that the Oct. 18 attack occurred while they were in the territory of Chen Mechan, another gang. He did not provide evidence; Haiti's government has said the four Salvadorans were abducted, and the Salvadoran government believes they are alive.

Joseph said he is upset that drone attacks are killing civilians in the area, with clashes intensifying ever since a U.N.-backed gang-suppression force working with Haitian police and soldiers, as well as Vectus Global — the private security firm founded by former U.S. Navy SEAL and Blackwater founder Erik Prince — began fighting armed men in Plaine du Cul-de-Sac near Port-au-Prince following the attack on the Salvadorans.

Joseph said that the same Haitian politicians who armed gangs in Haiti are bringing foreign troops "to destroy us."

He said he had a message for El Salvador's president, Nayib Bukele, who recently deployed 2,000 troops to Haiti: "The Haitian politicians are the father of the gangs and the rebels. ... The politicians don't want this to stop."

In his letter, Joseph wrote: "Given Mr. Nayib Bukele's vengeful remarks, expectations, and threats, I fear this situation will lead to an escalation of violence and a logic of reprisals, of which the Haitian people would be the first victims."

Questions swirl about oversight of El Salvador's troops

Joseph alleged in his interview with the AP that politicians are warning him about any security operations headed his way.

He added that he doesn't have a problem with forces arresting gang members, but he accused forces of dropping drones and killing children and the elderly.

Joseph said he's ready to have a dialogue and lay down guns, although when asked what he wanted in exchange, he declined to say, adding he would talk about that when he sits down with a peace commission. He also rejected accusations that 400 Mawozo has killed innocent Haitians.

In a statement late Monday, U.N. spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said they had received a letter with Joseph's signature: "However, receipt of such a letter does not constitute endorsement of its contents, recognition of its author, or a position by the United Nations."

He noted that the vast majority of Salvadoran military personnel are not deployed under the U.N.-backed gang suppression force, "and therefore fall outside" the U.N. mandate and reporting.

"We want to underscore that the United Nations remains concerned that communities continue to bear the brunt of the situation in Haiti," he said, adding that any type of security operation "must be carried out in full accordance with applicable international law."

Gang leader calls for a 'peaceful solution'

Joseph asserted in his letter that recent events in Plaine du Cul-de-Sac, especially where another gang, Chen Mechan, operates, "are causing serious concern."

Joseph wrote that he was "officially available" to receive the delegation that he "respectfully" requested and would "participate in any meeting aimed at finding a peaceful solution, a dialogue agreement and a sustainable stabilization process."

"I remain convinced that dialogue must prevail over force," he said. "The protection of civilians, particularly children and vulnerable families, must be at the heart of any international initiative," Joseph wrote.

More than 5,700 people have been killed or injured across Haiti from January to mid-September, according to the U.N.

In the two-page letter sent Nov. 1, Joseph said he has "officially raised the white flag" since Aug. 20 and seeks a "peaceful solution to the national crisis, in particular through the opening of a dialogue between the international forces present in Haiti and the 400 Mawozo group."

The group, which roughly translates to "400 Simpletons," operates largely in Croix-des-Bouquets, a community near Port-au-Prince. A spokesperson for the gang who declined to be identified accused the government of abandoning that area and asserted that's why Joseph took charge of it. The gang is known for carrying out kidnappings, including those in October 2021 of 17 missionaries , 16 of them from the U.S. and one from Canada. There were five children in that group, and all were eventually released.

The spokesperson denied they were kidnappings but rather a "justice" measure given sexual abuse charges against a former missionary. The spokesperson also said that 400 Mawozo is not a terrorist organization, and that young people lacking education who are allegedly being used by politicians are being killed.

The U.S. government has issued a $1 million reward for Joseph, who was indicted in the U.S. in 2022 on charges of hostage taking and conspiracy to commit hostage taking.

articles.title: Eleições nos EUA: quando sai o resultado? | G1
articles.standfirst: País não tem órgão como o TSE no Brasil, e regras para a apuração varia de estado para estado. Resultados definitivos sobre quem venceu as eleições podem demorar semanas.
articles.summary: País não tem órgão como o TSE no Brasil, e regras para a apuração varia de estado para estado. Resultados definitivos sobre quem venceu as eleições podem demorar semanas.
articles.body:
Milhares de eleitores vão às urnas nos Estados Unidos , nesta terça-feira (3), para as eleições de meio de mandato, que vai mostrar qual partido irá controlar a Câmara e o Senado pelos próximos dois anos. A votação é crucial para o presidente Donald Trump .

Os Estados Unidos não têm um órgão nacional como o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), responsável por coordenar as eleições em todo o país e totalizar os votos. Com isso, cada estado tem suas próprias regras.

Em geral, a apuração começa assim que os locais de votação fecham. O horário varia de estado para estado. Na Flórida, por exemplo, a votação termina às 19h. Em Nova York, os eleitores têm até as 21h. No Tennessee, o horário varia de acordo com o condado.

Em boa parte dos estados, a votação é feita em cédulas de papel. A contagem é feita por trabalhadores eleitorais, muitas vezes funcionários públicos. Tudo é fiscalizado pelos membros dos partidos políticos.

Em caso de diferenças de votos muito pequenas entre dois candidatos, os partidos ou a própria Justiça solicita que uma recontagem seja feita para certificar o vencedor.

Os primeiros resultados devem ser divulgados ainda na noite de terça-feira. No entanto, pode levar dias até que seja possível saber qual partido terá o controle da Câmara e do Senado.

Nas midterms de 2022, por exemplo, a disputa pelo controle da Câmara só foi definida mais de uma semana após a eleição. A demora ocorreu, entre outros fatores, porque alguns estados levam mais tempo para contar os votos enviados pelo correio.

Segundo a imprensa americana, campanhas arrecadaram mais de US$ 15 bilhões. Partidos investem para eleger deputados e senadores para o Congresso dos EUA.Como não há um órgão que centraliza a apuração de todo o país, esse trabalho costuma ser feito pela imprensa. Há quase 200 anos, a Associated Press é a principal fonte para agregar os dados das votações.

A agência espalha centenas de repórteres em locais de contagem de votos e vai coletando resultados oficiais.

Com base em dados estatísticos, a AP também costuma projetar quem venceu as eleições mesmo antes do fim da contagem dos votos.

Diferentemente do Brasil, o Congresso dos Estados Unidos é renovado parcialmente a cada dois anos. Quando ocorrem na metade do mandato presidencial, essas eleições são chamadas de midterms, ou eleições de meio de mandato.

Os deputados norte-americanos têm mandatos de dois anos, enquanto os senadores, de seis.

Com isso, a cada dois anos, o país renova toda a Câmara dos Representantes e cerca de um terço do Senado.

Sendo assim, desta vez, estarão em disputa todas as 435 cadeiras da Câmara e 35 das 100.

articles.title: Ford do Brasil faz recall de picape por falha na fixação dos bancos | G1
articles.standfirst: Modelos 2025 e 2026 da picape podem ter parafusos ausentes ou sem o aperto correto nos bancos dianteiros. Inspeção e solução do defeito demoram 25 minutos, segundo a Ford.
articles.summary: Modelos 2025 e 2026 da F-150 podem ter parafusos ausentes ou sem o aperto correto nos bancos dianteiros. Inspeção e solução do defeito demoram 25 minutos, segundo a Ford
articles.body:
Ford F-150 na versão Lariat. — Foto: Divulgação / Ford

A Ford anunciou nesta terça-feira (3) um recall da picape F-150, modelos 2025 e 2026, por uma falha na fixação dos bancos dianteiros .

O problema, de acordo com o comunicado, pode comprometer a proteção do motorista e do passageiro em uma colisão e aumentar o risco de lesões.

Segundo a fabricante, uma falha no processo de produção pode ter deixado os bancos sem alguns dos parafusos que os prendem à carroceria ou com essas peças sem o aperto adequado.

Nessas condições, os ocupantes podem perceber movimentação dos bancos ou ouvir ruídos durante a condução.

Em caso de colisão, o defeito pode afetar a estabilidade do banco e a posição de quem está sentado, prejudicando o funcionamento do cinto de segurança.

A campanha prevê a inspeção dos parafusos e, se necessário, o reaperto ou a substituição das peças . O serviço é gratuito e está disponível a partir desta terça-feira (3).

O recall abrange as unidades da F-150 com os chassis e as datas de produção abaixo:

Chassi: 1FTFW5L50SFC42333 / Data de produção: 7 de outubro de 2025

Chassi: 1FTFW5L59SFC42041 / Data de produção: 8 de outubro de 2025

Chassi: 1FTFW5L53SFC4186 9 / Data de produção: 10 de outubro de 2025

Chassi: 1FTFW5L54SFC60480 / Data de produção: 19 de novembro de 2025

Chassi: 1FTFW5L59SFC65383 / Data de produção: 19 de novembro de 2025

Chassi: 1FTFW5L51SFC63210 / Data de produção: 24 de novembro de 2025

Chassi: 1FTFW5L55SFC65140 / Data de produção: 26 de novembro de 2025

Chassi: 1FTFW4L56TFA43086 / Data de produção: 31 de janeiro de 2026

A previsão é de aproximadamente 25 minutos para a inspeção e, quando necessário, o reaperto ou a troca dos parafusos. O tempo pode variar conforme o fluxo de atendimento da concessionária . A Ford orienta os proprietários a atenderem imediatamente à convocação.

articles.title: Denúncias de violência contra animais crescem no Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Na capital, registros aumentaram 13%, com maior concentração em bairros da Zona Oeste. Denúncias podem ser feitas 24 horas por dia, de forma anônima.
articles.summary: As denúncias de violência contra animais cresceram no Rio de Janeiro em comparação com o ano passado. Antes do fim do ano, a central Linha Verde recebeu quase 16 mil denúncias.
articles.body:
As denúncias de violência contra animais cresceram no Rio de Janeiro em comparação com o ano passado. Antes mesmo do fim do ano, a central Linha Verde, do Disque Denúncia, recebeu quase 16 mil queixas. Ao longo de 2025, foram registradas mais de 14 mil ocorrências.

Maltratar animais é crime, com pena de um ano de prisão.

“Só na capital, houve um aumento de 13%, com maior concentração nos bairros da Zona Oeste, como Campo Grande, Jacarepaguá, Santa Cruz, Guaratiba, Bangu e Realengo. Qualquer cidadão pode denunciar 24 horas por dia, garantimos o anonimato”, afirmou Renato Almeida, diretor-geral do Disque Denúncia.

Rio registra quase 16 mil denúncias de maus-tratos contra animais — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

Além dos maus-tratos, o abandono também tem consequências para a vida urbana. A protetora Adriana Rosa, que resgata animais há 15 anos, afirma que o problema é também uma questão de saúde pública.

“A gente faz tudo por conta própria. Só eu mesmo estou com 70 aqui. Sete em hospedagem, pois não consigo colocar mais animais aqui, não se dão com outros e tem protetores com 100 e até 300 animais. E a gente fica devendo tudo. Só eu estou devendo umas três clínicas”, disse.

O cão Bolt foi abandonado. Uma câmera de segurança registrou o momento que ele foi deixado para trás — Foto: Diógenes Melquíades/ TV Globo

Bolt, um dos cães que vivem no abrigo “Toda Vida Importa”, em Guaratiba, na Zona Oeste do Rio, foi abandonado na rua. Câmeras de segurança registraram o momento em que um homem desceu de um carro e abriu a porta traseira.

O cachorro foi retirado do veículo e saiu correndo pela calçada. O homem caminhou pela rua e, 15 minutos depois, voltou ao automóvel. Bolt correu atrás do carro, mas foi deixado para trás.

“O que aconteceu com o Bolt é muito mais comum do que as pessoas imaginam. O problema é que as pessoas não checam as câmeras do local, acabam não sabendo o que ocorre ou deixam para lá. Mas pessoas que abandonam, pessoas de carro que simplesmente abandonam na rua e, normalmente, longe de casa, acontece muito”, afirmou a protetora Ana Paula Lima.

No sítio onde funciona a instituição vivem 1,2 mil cães e gatos. Cerca de 450 animais considerados mais tranquilos ficam soltos pelo terreno. Muitos dos que vivem no local foram abandonados ou sofreram maus-tratos.

O espaço é alugado e mantido por meio de doações. Equilibrar as contas é um desafio, segundo os responsáveis pelo abrigo, já que novos animais chegam todos os dias.

“O animal é dedicação, é cuidado, tudo isso. E as pessoas esquecem disso. Animal não é objeto. São eternas crianças. Olha quanto amor eu tenho aqui”, disse Ana Paula.

Quem testemunhar casos de agressão contra animais pode fazer uma denúncia à Linha Verde do Disque Denúncia pelo telefone (21) 2253-1177. O anonimato é garantido.

Protetores lutam para manter abrigos de animais abertos no Rio — Foto: Diógenes Melquíades/ TV Globo

articles.title: Cobrança de Zona Azul é retomada em Itajubá após 3 meses suspensa | G1
articles.standfirst: Sistema passa por período de testes e cobrança a partir de 16 de novembro. Valor será de R$ 3 por hora.
articles.summary: Sistema passa por período de testes e cobrança a partir de 16 de novembro. Valor será de R$ 3 por hora.
articles.body:
Itajubá retoma cobrança de Zona Azul — Foto: Arquivo

O estacionamento rotativo, conhecido como Zona Azul, voltou a funcionar em Itajubá em 1º de novembro, três meses após ser suspenso. A tarifa será de R$ 3 por hora.

Os primeiros 15 dias serão de adaptação, sem cobrança, para que os motoristas conheçam o novo sistema. A tarifa começa a ser cobrada em 16 de novembro.

A retomada da cobrança ocorre após a suspensão temporária do serviço em 3 de agosto de 2026. Na ocasião, a prefeitura informou que a interrupção era necessária para regularizar a prestação do serviço por meio de um novo processo de licitação.

Os motoristas poderão pagar pelo estacionamento pelo aplicativo Mobitt ou por meio do QR Code disponível nas placas instaladas nas ruas. O pagamento poderá ser feito via Pix ou cartão de crédito.

A orientação da Prefeitura é que os condutores aproveitem o período de testes para baixar o aplicativo, fazer o cadastro e registrar os veículos. Depois de estacionar, o motorista terá 15 minutos para efetuar o pagamento do tíquete.

Segundo o diretor de Mobilidade Urbana de Itajubá, Márcio Rogério da Silva Faria, o tempo foi estabelecido para facilitar o acesso ao serviço e evitar problemas durante a operação.

"É para assegurar que ele possa concretizar este pagamento de forma segura. Por exemplo, às vezes uma instabilidade na rede de internet do próprio usuário ou ele ter de se deslocar até um ponto de vendas para realizar o pagamento", afirmou.

A fiscalização será feita por agentes de trânsito e também terá o apoio de um veículo que irá circular pelas ruas e identificar, por meio de georreferenciamento, se as vagas estão sendo utilizadas de acordo com as regras do estacionamento rotativo.

Quem tiver dificuldade para utilizar o aplicativo poderá contar com orientadores próximos às áreas da Zona Azul. Também haverá pontos de venda em estabelecimentos comerciais credenciados.

articles.title: Nicole Taylor, do trio Taylor Red, morre aos 35 anos após diagnóstico de câncer de mama | G1
articles.standfirst: O anúncio foi feito pelas irmãs gêmeas da artista, Nika e Natalie Taylor, com quem formava o trio country.
articles.summary: O anúncio foi feito pelas irmãs gêmeas da artista, Nika e Natalie Taylor, com quem formava o trio country.
articles.body:
Natalie, Nika e Nikole Taylor, do trio Taylor Red, em imagem de abril de 2025 — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Nicole Taylor, do trio de música country Taylor Red, morreu aos 35 anos. O anúncio foi feito pelas irmãs gêmeas de Nicole, Nika e Natalie, nesta segunda-feira (2).

Segundo elas, a irmã, que foi diagnosticada com câncer de mama em estágio 3 ainda em 2022, morreu em 28 de setembro.

"Estamos com o coração partido ao anunciar o falecimento da nossa irmã, Nicole Taylor. Sinceramente, achávamos que ela seria curada aqui na Terra, mas agora ela está curada no céu", afirmou Nika em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais.

As irmãs contaram que o tipo de câncer de Nicole era bastante agressivo, mas que a cantora “encarou isso sem medo”. “Ela afirmou: 'Não vamos viver aterrorizados durante todo esse processo'. Ela até praticou CrossFit enquanto fazia quimioterapia. Ela respondeu bem aos tratamentos e foi declarada livre de sinais da doença."

"Ela tentou não viver com medo e manteve-se muito esperançosa. Viajou, buscou aproveitar a vida, trabalhou bastante e procurou se divertir", contou Natalie.

Quando o câncer de Nicole evoluiu parra grau 4, os médicos relataram que Nicole teria, no máximo, mais três meses de vida. Mas Nicole vivei cerca de um ano após o prognóstico.

"Ainda estamos processando tudo. Sinceramente, é muito difícil falar sobre isso, mas vamos fazer o nosso melhor para compartilhar a história dela", contou Natalie.

Criado em 2010, o trio Taylor Red é conhecido por canções como "Country Money" e "Rent Free". Além de cantoras, as irmãs são compositoras e multi-instrumentistas.

articles.title: Trecho da MT-251 ficará parcialmente interditado por 25 dias; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Bloqueio começa nesta terça-feira (3), para obras de construção de rotatória e acesso ao Contorno Leste.
articles.summary: Bloqueio começa nesta terça-feira (3), para obras de construção de rotatória e acesso ao Contorno Leste.
articles.body:
A restrição será feita apenas na pista no sentido Cuiabá-Chapada dos Guimarães. O trecho já recebeu sinalização e redutores de velocidade para orientar os motoristas. — Foto: Sinfra-MT

Um trecho de aproximadamente 500 metros da MT-251, que liga Cuiabá a Chapada dos Guimarães , funcionará em meia pista a partir desta terça-feira (3) . A interdição parcial deve durar 25 dias e será necessária para a construção de uma rotatória e de um acesso ao Contorno Leste, próximo à Fundação Bradesco, em Cuiabá (veja imagem acima) .

A restrição será feita apenas na pista no sentido Cuiabá-Chapada dos Guimarães. O trecho já recebeu sinalização e redutores de velocidade para orientar os motoristas. articles.title: Mário Gattinho: Campinas contrata médicos por R$ 1,5 milhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Contrato sem licitação prevê profissionais de terapia intensiva pediátrica e cirurgia pediátrica. Segundo a prefeitura, medida é necessária após aposentadorias e exonerações de médicos.
articles.summary: Mário Gattinho em Campinas terá serviços de UTI e cirurgia pediátrica via contrato emergencial para suprir plantões após aposentadorias e saídas de médicos.
articles.body:
Unidade Pediátrica Mário Gattinho, em Campinas (SP) — Foto: Carlos Bassan/Prefeitura de Campinas

A Rede Mário Gatti, responsável pelos hospitais municipais de Campinas (SP), autorizou uma contratação emergencial de R$ 1.568.340 para serviços médicos de terapia intensiva pediátrica e cirurgia pediátrica na unidade Mário Gattinho.

A medida foi publicada no Diário Oficial desta terça-feira (3) e será realizada sem licitação.

Segundo a prefeitura, a contratação é necessária para cobrir plantões após a saída de médicos concursados por aposentadoria ou exoneração . O contrato deve começar ainda em novembro e terá duração inicial de até seis meses, com possibilidade de prorrogação por mais seis.

A empresa escolhida foi a Sanklech Serviços Médicos Ltda. De acordo com a Rede Mário Gatti, oito empresas apresentaram propostas, e a selecionada ofereceu o menor preço.

Segundo a administração municipal, serão contratadas entre 45 e 60 horas médicas por mês , conforme a necessidade dos plantões.

Por que a contratação será feita sem licitação?

A Rede Mário Gatti informou que a contratação emergencial será usada até a conclusão de uma licitação regular, prevista para ocorrer entre o fim de 2026 e o início de 2027 . O processo ainda está na fase de pesquisa de preços.

A administração justificou a dispensa de licitação por se tratar de um serviço essencial, que precisa ser mantido enquanto a seleção definitiva não é concluída.

Segundo a Rede Mário Gatti, todos os procedimentos administrativos e legais foram seguidos. A autorização foi assinada pelo diretor-presidente da instituição, Sérgio Bisogni, em 29 de outubro.

articles.title: Commotio cordis: entenda possível causa de morte de jogador espanhol | G1
articles.standfirst: Atacante sofreu uma parada cardíaca depois de uma forte colisão com o goleiro adversário e chegou a ser reanimado em campo. O quadro neurológico piorou e ele acabou não resistindo.
articles.summary: Atacante sofreu uma parada cardíaca depois de uma forte colisão com o goleiro adversário e chegou a ser reanimado em campo. O quadro neurológico piorou e ele acabou não resistindo.
articles.body:
Após uma forte colisão com o goleiro do time adversário, o atacante Jesús de Miguel, do time espanhol Tenerife, sofreu uma parada cardíaca e caiu desacordado no campo. Apesar de ter sido reanimado, sua morte foi confirmada na manhã desta terça-feira (3) .

Segundo especialistas, a principal suspeita da causa da morte é conhecida como commotio cordis , expressão em latim que significa agito no coração.

➡️A commotio cordis é um quadro raro e grave que apode acontecer após um impacto repentino no tórax. De acordo com a American Heart Association, o golpe físico pode interromper os batimentos cardíacos e causar uma parada cardíaca súbita .

Jesús de Miguel se choca com goleiro Owono e tem parada cardíaca na Espanha. — Foto: Reprodução

Antonio Carlos Avanza, presidente do Departamento de Ergometria, Exercício, Cardiologia Nuclear e Reabilitação Cardiovascular da Sociedade Brasileira de Cardiologia (SBC), explica que não necessariamente a pancada precisa ser tão forte, porque o quadro depende do ciclo cardíaco.

"Às vezes você não tem uma fratura, pode ser uma pancada menor, uma joelhada, uma bolada não tão intensa, mas que se pega no momento de uma alteração eletrofisiológica, leva a uma arrtimia cardíaca e a uma parada", detalha.

No caso de Jesús Miguel, o atleta chegou a ser atendido e reanimado em campo, levado ao hospital, mas o quadro neurológico piorou e ele não resistiu. (entenda mais abaixo)

Quadros semelhantes aconteceram em esportes de maior impacto, como o futebol americano. Foi o caso do jogador Damar Hamlin, em 2023 , que também precisou ser reanimado após um choque em uma partida da NFL.

O atacante do FC Tenerife, Jesús de Miguel, à esquerda, duela pela bola durante uma partida de futebol contra Andorra em Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Espanha, segunda-feira, 2 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: AP Photo

Por se tratar de uma quadro grave, a rapidez no atendimento é essencial para garantir a sobrevivência do paciente.

"O soccoro tem que chegar nesse paciente em no máximo três minutos. Senão, nós podemos não conseguir reanimá-lo e levar a uma situação de lesões neurológicas irreversíveis", comenta Avanza.

Jesús foi reanimado em campo após a parada respiratória e internado para acompanhamento do jogador, mas o quadro neurológico piorou ao longo da madrugada e o atleta faleceu na manhã desta terça.

Avanza explica que as consequências neurológicas acontecem pela quantidade insuficiente de oxigêncio que chega aos tecidos e células do corpo, condição conhecida como hipóxia .

"Em uma parada cardíaca, o coração para momentaneamente de bombear sangue para o corpo inteiro, inclusive para o cérebro. O dano neurológico pode acontecer porque as células do cérebro são muito sensíveis, e sem oxigênio, pode acontecer a morte de células nervosas", detalha.

Dependendo do local afetado, o dano cerebral pode ser irreversível, levando à morte.

A Casa Branca anunciou nesta terça-feira (3) que a primeira-dama dos Estados Unidos, Melania Trump , reunirá pessoalmente representantes da Rússia e da Ucrânia juntos em Washington.

Segundo a agência de notícias Reuters, o encontro está marcado para esta quinta-feira (5). Não foram divulgadas quais autoridades participarão da reunião.

Oleshky encontrava-se sob ocupação de tropas russas desde fevereiro de 2022, enfrentando uma severa crise humanitária e de abastecimento. A população remanescente, composta em sua maioria por idosos, enfrentava escassez crítica de alimentos, água potável, remédios e atendimento médico.

A trégua humanitária temporária negociada por Melania entrou em vigor no dia 29 de outubro de 2026 e terminou em 1º de novembro.

articles.title: Rio Tapajós em Santarém atinge 1,30m e se aproxima da cota de alerta | G1
articles.standfirst: Após uma semana de variações, nível chegou a 1,30 metro nesta terça-feira (3); cidade enfrenta quase quatro meses sem chuva e período de queimadas.
articles.summary: Rio Tapajós em Santarém registra fenômeno de repiquete e atinge 1,30 metro nesta terça-feira, enquanto a cidade enfrenta estiagem prolongada e queimadas no Pará.
articles.body:
Nível do Rio Tapajós voltou a baixar nesta terça-feira (3). — Foto: Marcos Santos

O nível do Rio Tapajós voltou a recuar em Santarém , no oeste do Pará, depois de apresentar uma sequência de pequenas elevações nos últimos dias. Nesta terça-feira (3), o rio atingiu a marca de 1,30 metro, ficando 80 centímetros abaixo da cota de alerta, que é de 2,10 metros. A oscilação ocorre em meio a um período de estiagem que já se aproxima de quatro meses no município.

Os dados são do boletim diário divulgado pela Defesa Civil Municipal. A medição é feita na régua da Agência Nacional de Águas (ANA), instalada no porto da Companhia Docas do Pará (CDP).

No dia 26 de outubro, o nível estava em 1,38 metro. No dia seguinte, subiu para 1,42 metro e, em 28 de outubro, recuou para 1,40 metro. A marca permaneceu a mesma no dia 29 e voltou a subir para 1,43 metro em 30 de outubro. No dia 31, caiu para 1,41 metro.

Em 1º de novembro, o rio chegou a 1,46 metro, mas voltou a baixar no dia seguinte, quando marcou 1,41 metro. Nesta terça-feira (3), a medição apontou nova queda, para 1,30 metro.

A oscilação do nível do rio é conhecida como repiquete, fenômeno hidrológico comum na bacia amazônica. Ele ocorre quando um rio que está em processo de vazante ou enchente interrompe temporariamente essa tendência e apresenta uma elevação repentina, que pode durar pouco tempo, antes de voltar a baixar ou subir.

Na comparação com os anos anteriores, a marca registrada nesta terça-feira está 90 centímetros abaixo do nível observado no mesmo período de 2025. Por outro lado, está 1,27 metro acima do registro de 2024 e 90 centímetros acima da marca de 2023.

Santarém enfrenta um período prolongado de tempo seco. A última chuva registrada na cidade ocorreu em 23 de julho. A falta de precipitações também preocupa em razão do cenário de queimadas que atinge o município e outras áreas do oeste do Pará.

A previsão para esta terça-feira indica sol entre muitas nuvens, com períodos de céu nublado e temperatura entre 25°C e 34°C. Não há previsão de chuva para o dia.

articles.body: VIJAYAWADA: Cyclone Murasu has triggered extremely heavy rainfall, inundation and disruption to normal life across parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh, with Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam and Palnadu among the affected districts. Guntur district recorded the highest rainfall among urban local bodies, with Ponnur receiving 312.76 mm, followed by Guntur city at 298.36 mm. Several other towns in the coastal belt also experienced very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall.Bapatla district recorded the highest average rainfall among all districts at 56.95 mm during the 24-hour period from 8.30 am on November 2 to 7 am on November 3. Prakasam recorded 32.15 mm, Guntur 26.59 mm and Palnadu 4.01 mm during the same period. The figures indicate that the cyclone's impact was concentrated over the southern and central coastal districts, with intense localised downpours causing inundation in several locations.The preliminary assessment by the Agriculture Department also points to substantial crop exposure, particularly in paddy and cotton fields. Across 15 districts, about 30,661 hectares of paddy and 21,474 hectares of cotton at vulnerable crop stages have been identified as potentially affected. However, these are preliminary estimates of expected damage. A separate field-level report has confirmed crop inundation across 5,969 hectares in two districts, including 5,619 hectares in Bapatla alone.The crop-wise assessment shows that the potential damage is not confined to paddy. Cotton accounts for 21,474 hectares, or 18.4% of the area under cultivation at vulnerable stages, with Palnadu alone accounting for 14,980 hectares and Markapuram for 4,417 hectares. Maize damage is estimated at 605 hectares, with Prakasam accounting for about 343 hectares. The Agriculture Department has cautioned that these estimates are preliminary and will require field verification.In Bapatla, inundation was reported across 16 villages, affecting 9,600 farmers. Around 5,600 hectares of paddy and 19 hectares of blackgram were reported inundated. East Godavari reported another 350 hectares of crop inundation across 19 villages, affecting 466 farmers. The combined preliminary inundation figure stands at 5,969 hectares across 35 villages.Prakasam district reported the highest impact, with 99,899 people from 30,895 households affected across eight mandals and 27 villages. Bapatla reported 25,788 people affected across 25 villages in 10 mandals, while Krishna district reported 9,205 people affected across 120 villages and 14 mandals. In Palnadu, 573 households were listed as affected across three mandals. Guntur reported 252 people affected in three villages. Across the state, 1.75 lakh people from 44,651 households were covered in the preliminary impact assessment.The preliminary damage assessment also reported 39 instances of inundation across the districts, of which 28 had been rectified and 11 were pending. As many as 112 electric poles were identified as damaged, with only one reported as rectified at the time of assessment. The report also recorded 71 uprooted trees, of which 69 had been cleared. No human casualties, house damage or livestock losses had been confirmed in the initial assessment.The Agriculture Department's estimates cover crops at different stages, including flowering, grain filling, maturity and harvesting. Paddy damage is estimated at 30,661 hectares, accounting for 5.7% of the 5.33 lakh hectares under vulnerable crop stages. articles.title: In September, inmates at an Ohio jail began drawing portraits of overlooked shelter dogs; two months later, 18 of the 20 dogs featured in the artwork have found homes, giving both animals and artists a second chance
articles.summary: If you ever visit a busy animal shelter, you naturally start noticing certain facts like the breed, size, age, how loud a bark is, it all happens
articles.body: If you ever visit a busy animal shelter, you naturally start noticing certain facts like the breed, size, age, how loud a bark is, it all happens subconsciously, and in a matter of seconds. But at the Franklin County Dog Shelter in Columbus, Ohio, visitors walking past the kennels have been stopping for a very different reason: hand-drawn portraits taped right next to the metal doors. Since last autumn, inmates at the Franklin County Corrections Center have been using pencils, paper, and careful observation to sketch dogs waiting for adoption, reported The Washington Post. It is an unlikely partnership between two county institutions that rarely share headlines, but the early numbers tell a striking story. Within roughly two months of launching the initiative, 18 of the first 20 dogs featured in the artwork had already been adopted into permanent homes. Read more about this heart-warming gesture, as reported by The Washington Post, here:The Herbie effectTake James Bowshier and his wife as an example. They walked into the shelter with a clear plan in mind: look for a puppy. But as they browsed the runs, a drawing hanging outside one of the kennels caught James’s eye. The portrait showed Herbie, a one-year-old pit bull mix, captured with a level of warmth and detail that made him stand out from the rows of surrounding cages.That single sketch did what standard kennel cards rarely manage to do; it forced the couple to slow down. Instead of sweeping past to look for younger animals, they paused, took a closer look, and asked shelter staff if they could meet Herbie in person. They ended up taking him home that very day. Without that drawing breaking through the noise of the shelter floor, Herbie might easily have been passed over.Humanising the dog shelterShelters are demanding, high-volume environments. Staff members and volunteers work endlessly to manage intakes, medical care, and public visits, but they can only spend so much time introducing each dog to potential adopters. Meanwhile, kennels are inherently loud and stressful. Even the gentlest dog can come across as overly anxious, hyperactive, or completely withdrawn when viewed through wire mesh.Standard kennel tags list crucial information: intake dates, breed estimates, and basic medical history. Valuable as those facts are, they can inadvertently reduce a living animal to an administrative case file. A hand-drawn portrait shifts that dynamic immediately. It tells potential adopters that someone sat down, studied this specific animal's features, and cared enough to translate their personality onto paper. It transforms a quick glance into a moment of genuine human connection.A sense of purpose behind barsThe impact of the project flows both ways. For the artists inside the Franklin County Corrections Center, drawing shelter dogs offers something that can be notoriously hard to find in custody: tangible purpose and a real link to the outside community.Daily life in a correctional facility is heavily structured and offers few opportunities to make a constructive public contribution. Working on these portraits requires patience, steady focus, and hours of quiet concentration. More importantly, it gives participants a chance to create something that actually leaves the facility and serves a clear, positive good. Their work hangs in a public space, helps animals find families, and often ends up framed on the wall of an adopter's living room.No one is claiming that drawing dogs is a cure-all for criminal justice reform or that it solves systemic issues on its own. What it does provide, however, is practical, humane engagement. It allows people in jail to be recognised for their skill and effort rather than solely defined by their current circumstances.Creative solutions don't need to be complexIt is worth keeping a realistic perspective. A nice drawing cannot replace responsible adoption practices. Bringing a pet into a home requires time, money, proper space, and an honest assessment of whether the animal fits a family's lifestyle. Shelter workers still need to facilitate proper meet-and-greets, discuss behavioral needs, and ensure lasting matches. The artwork simply serves as an invitation; the real work of adoption comes after.Still, what makes this project so compelling is its sheer simplicity. It didn't require high-tech tools, massive funding grants, or complicated administrative overhauls. It just took sketch pads, drawing pencils, cooperation between two local agencies, and a willingness to try something different.By helping prospective adopters see shelter dogs as individuals with stories worth hearing, and by giving incarcerated artists a meaningful way to contribute, a simple sheet of paper has managed to change the trajectory for dozens of lives on both sides of the shelter fence.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A 26-year-old Australian man won A$1 million on Thursday after catching a red-tagged barramundi during a fishing trip with his younger brother in the
articles.body: A 26-year-old Australian man won A$1 million on Thursday after catching a red-tagged barramundi during a fishing trip with his younger brother in the Northern Territory. Matthew Maurice, from Darwin, caught the fishat Corroboree Billabong, where it measured just over 80cm. He became only the second person to win the top prize in the Million Dollar Fish competition's 12-year history.Maurice had gone fishing with his younger brother, who was visiting from overseas. The brothers had planned to spend a quiet evening together on the water. Maurice, who regularly participates in the competition, was using a suspended jerkbait when a barramundi took his lure. Within seconds, the fish jumped out of the water, revealing a bright red tag. He realised that it could be one of the fish released as part of the competition."I saw the fish jump within the first 10 seconds and spotted a bright red tag hanging out of it," Maurice said, according to ABC News Australia. "There was about two minutes of absolute panic and then I don't actually remember netting it. It was probably the most stressful two minutes of my life," he added.The million-dollar winThe brothers were fishing at Corroboree Billabong, a popular fishing location east of Darwin. Maurice had been talking with his brother when the fish took his lure.The red tag immediately caught his attention. When he saw that it carried the words "Season 12", he became nervous. He later recalled that his legs were shaking as he tried to bring the fish in.People on a nearby houseboat also noticed and began cheering for the brothers. After about two minutes, they managed to land the barramundi.The fish was the only barramundi carrying the A$1 million prize tag in the competition's 12th season. Its capture made Maurice the second person to claim the competition's biggest prize.Maurice said he was still struggling to believe what had happened. "It's surreal. I feel like I'm in a dream," he said.He added, "I'm just happy to catch fish. I can't believe I caught a million dollars' worth of fish. Any barra is a good barra, especially the million-dollar one."'I'm a millionaire, Mum'After learning about his win, Maurice called his family to share the news. His first call was to his mother, who was outside a pub when she heard that her son had become a millionaire. "I'm a millionaire, Mum," he told her. His mother replied, "I'm standing outside the pub and people are looking at me." Maurice then asked her not to go back inside and tell everyone about the win.His father was equally surprised when he received the news. Maurice had to reassure him that he was serious about winning the money. "I swear Dad, I am dead-set serious right now," he said. His father responded, "I'm so proud of you," before adding, "You're set for life."Maurice has already thought about how he might use the prize. He said he wanted to make sensible decisions rather than spend the money immediately. "I don't think I should be allowed to touch the money. Someone else might need to look after it for me," he said.He added that he would probably buy a house, clear any outstanding payments and spend a small amount on himself.Second A$1 million winner in 12 yearsThe Million Dollar Fish competition was introduced to encourage tourists and recreational fishers to visit Australia's Northern Territory, particularly during the quieter wet season.The competition offers cash prizes for catching specially tagged barramundi. Season 12 began with one fish carrying the A$1 million prize and 100 others worth A$10,000 each.Before Maurice's win, only one person had claimed the top prize. Keegan Payne, a teenager from Katherine, caught the first million-dollar barramundi in April 2024, shortly before the ninth season ended.According to the Northern Territory government, the competition has awarded more than A$2.47 million in prize money since it began.Maurice's catch will also result in an additional A$10,000 donation to Surf Life Saving NT, the competition's official charity partner. Total charitable donations associated with the competition have now exceeded A$133,000.Although the only million-dollar fish for Season 12 has now been caught, the competition is not over. Another 96 tagged barramundi, each worth A$10,000, remain available to be caught across the Northern Territory. The current season will continue until March 31, 2027.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1610, Galileo revealed four moons of Jupiter, but another astronomer called them an illusion; their opposing books survived bound together for centuries before the rare volume sold for Rs 2.07 crore in 2026
articles.summary: Galileo Galilei is a name that needs no introduction.
articles.body: Galileo Galilei is a name that needs no introduction. In 1610, Italian astronomer Galileo published a small book that challenged the way people understood the universe. He used a telescope and observed four bodies moving around Jupiter, providing evidence that not everything in the universe revolved around Earth.However, it’s normal that people generally are not convinced with anything that challenges their notion or age-old beliefs. Among those who challenged his findings was astronomer Francesco Sizzi, who argued that the supposed moons were optical illusions produced by the telescope.Now over 400 years later, the books documenting these opposing views have become part of an extraordinary story of scientific discovery.Rs 2.07 crore bookIn February 2026, a rare volume containing Galileo’s landmark publication alongside three other early works on astronomy and optics sold at Christie’s for US$217,600, approximately Rs 2.07 crore. It was a collection that was offered as part of the auction house’s sale of fine printed books, manuscripts and science.The little book that changed astronomyThe book was published in Venice in March 1610. Galileo’s Sidereus Nuncius, commonly translated as The Starry Messenger, announced observations that had become possible through the relatively new technology of the telescope.Galileo learnt about the development of the telescope in 1609 and later built his own improved instruments. By the end of that year, he was using them to observe the night sky. In January 1610, he turned his attention to Jupiter and noticed several points of light near the planet. As he continued observing them on successive nights, their changing positions revealed that they were orbiting Jupiter rather than remaining fixed among the stars.It was a significant discovery as it challenged the established Aristotelian picture of the universe. As per his theory, the heavens were understood through a system of nested celestial spheres and Earth occupied a central position.In Sidereus Nuncius, Galileo also described the Moon’s uneven and mountainous surface. It also mentioned that the Milky Way has numerous individual stars that could not be distinguished with the naked eye.Now this book made Galileo famous across Europe.The astronomer who refused to believeHowever, Francesco Sizzi, a contemporary of Galileo, refused to believe his theory and questioned the existence of Jupiter’s newly reported moons.The existence of other bodies orbiting a planet questioned the order in which celestial movements were interpreted. Sizzi argued that the appearances Galileo described could be produced by the telescope itself.The disagreement is particularly intriguing because the two positions survived together in the same physical volume. Sizzi’s Dianoia astronomica, optica, physica, published in Venice in 1611, was bound alongside Galileo’s Sidereus Nuncius in the copy later sold by Christie’s.According to Christie’s catalogue, Galileo, in turn, declined to refute Sizzi, preferring to preserve their friendship. The episode offers a glimpse of a time when new scientific observations confronted long-established beliefs, and the debate over evidence was still unfolding.Four books, one volume and centuries of historyThe copy sold in 2026 was more than a first edition of Galileo’s celebrated work. It was a Sammelband, a volume in which separate publications were bound together. Alongside Sidereus Nuncius were three other first editions published in 1611.The second work was Sizzi’s response to the controversy over Jupiter’s moons. The third, by Marcus Antonius de Dominis, explored vision, light, lenses and the rainbow, with material on the telescope added amid the excitement surrounding Galileo’s discoveries. The fourth, by Giovanni Antonio Magini, explored the properties and effects of spherical concave mirrors.According to Christie’s catalogue, the works were bound in contemporary stiff vellum boards. The volume also contains a reused sheet from a 1474 edition of a Latin translation of Herodotus, incorporated into the inside cover. Its binding and surviving details offer a glimpse into how early printed books were assembled and preserved.From a disputed discovery to an astronomical legacyThe four moons Galileo observed are now known as Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto.Galileo recorded the changing positions of the points of light over successive nights and recognised that their movement was evidence of their orbit around Jupiter. What initially appeared to be an arrangement of distant stars became evidence that celestial bodies could revolve around a world other than Earth.When the rare volume sold for US$217,600 in 2026, its significance lay in this unusual combination of scientific achievement and intellectual resistance.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Indiana doctor cut her hours to care for her newborn and reported earning $6,677 a week, but her divorce court calculated her earning capacity at $8,811 a week; an appeals court has upheld the ruling
articles.summary: An Indiana doctor who reduced her working hours to care for her newborn daughter has lost her appeal against a divorce court's decision to calculate her
articles.body: An Indiana doctor who reduced her working hours to care for her newborn daughter has lost her appeal against a divorce court's decision to calculate her weekly earning capacity at $8,811, despite her reporting an income of $6,677 a week. The Indiana Court of Appeals ruled on Thursday siad that the lower court had sufficient evidence to conclude that Aiza Ashraf, a radiologist, was capable of working full-time. The judges also upheld an order allowing her former husband, Mohsin Mukhtar, to spend three nights a week with their young daughter.Ashraf and Mukhtar, both radiologists employed by Indiana University, married in 2018 and welcomed their daughter in August 2024, according to the case details available on Justia. Ashraf filed for divorce the following month. The couple's separation led to disagreements over their daughter's care, parenting time, and the income that should be considered when calculating child support.Both doctors received payments from Indiana University for teaching and from IU Health for providing medical services. They also had opportunities to earn additional money by taking extra shifts, commonly referred to as "moonlighting". Before taking maternity leave, Ashraf earned the same base salary as her husband.However, in January 2025, Ashraf reduced her workload to three-quarters of a full-time schedule to look after their daughter. She told the court that her gross weekly income was $6,677. Mukhtar argued that she could still earn the same base salary as him if she returned to full-time work.Why court calculated income higherDuring the divorce proceedings, Ashraf explained that she specialised in breast imaging radiology and planned to maintain her credentials in that field rather than general diagnostic radiology.She said opportunities for additional shifts were limited because breast imaging was generally performed during regular working hours.Mukhtar disagreed. He told the court that both had the same employment contract and that Ashraf retained the training, qualifications and licence needed to perform general radiology work.He asked the court to calculate both parents' weekly income at $8,811, excluding earnings from additional shifts.On October 13, last year, the Hamilton Circuit Court accepted that Ashraf could work full-time and assessed her earning capacity at $8,811 per week.Ashraf challenged the decision, arguing that she had reduced her hours to care for her daughter rather than to avoid financial responsibilities.The appeals court examined whether the lower court had acted improperly by using her potential earnings instead of her reported income.Under Indiana's child support rules, courts can consider what a parent is capable of earning when that parent is voluntarily unemployed or working fewer hours than their qualifications and opportunities would allow.The appeals judges noted that Ashraf had acknowledged she could work additional hours if she wanted. They also considered evidence that she previously earned the same base salary as Mukhtar.The court rejected her argument that the $8,811 figure improperly included her husband's additional earnings. Both parents' financial documents identified that amount as his base weekly pay, excluding extra shifts.Dispute over overnight stays with fatherThe case also involved a disagreement over how much time Mukhtar should spend with their daughter. According to the judgment, both parents initially helped care for the baby after her birth. However, in September 2024, Ashraf began sleeping in the nursery and prevented Mukhtar from entering the room.A preliminary court order issued in December 2024 did not allow overnight stays with the father. It provided that he could request them when the child turned six months old or began eating solid food.Mukhtar subsequently requested more time with his daughter, but Ashraf refused. On one occasion, she left the child with her maternal grandmother in Texas for two nights rather than arrange overnight care with Mukhtar.At the final divorce hearing in March 2025, Ashraf proposed gradually increasing the father's parenting time, with overnight stays beginning when their daughter turned two.She explained that she intended to continue breastfeeding until that age and wanted to be available to comfort the child at night.Mukhtar sought equal parenting time, including overnight stays. He told the court that he had participated in the baby's early care, regularly exercised his permitted parenting time and completed parenting courses.The lower court eventually awarded him three days of parenting time each week, including overnight stays.Appeals court upholds both decisionsAshraf challenged the overnight arrangement, arguing that the immediate increase from no overnight stays to three per week was not in their daughter's best interests.The appeals court acknowledged that the arrangement went beyond the usual recommendations under Indiana's parenting time guidelines for young children.However, it found that the lower court had considered the circumstances of the family, including Mukhtar's involvement in childcare, his completion of parenting courses and his ability to provide suitable accommodation.The judges also considered the lower court's concern that a gradual increase in parenting time might not happen because Ashraf had previously refused additional visits. The appeals court therefore concluded that the lower court had sufficient grounds to approve the arrangement.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Billionaire Mark Cuban’s message to GenZ, listen to Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' advice: I always tell young people, 'Go work at ...'
articles.summary: Mark Cuban wants young workers to stop waiting for perfection.
articles.body: Mark Cuban wants young workers to stop waiting for perfection. The billionaire investor said an ordinary first job can help graduates build experience and demonstrate responsibility. His advice echoes that of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who worked at McDonald’s as a teenager. According to Fortune, Bezos highlighted the benefits of that experience in a 2025 interview.“I always advise young people: Go work at McDonald’s,” Bezos said. “You learn responsibility. You learn how to show up. You learn how to deal with people. You learn how to hustle.” Cuban made a similar argument on a recent episode of The Diary of a CEO. He said, “Don’t get the perfect job because those are hard to find. Just get a job.” Both emphasised developing practical skills rather than waiting for an ideal role.Why Mark Cuban says an ordinary job can helpBefore building his technology fortune, Cuban worked jobs such as selling rubbish bags, slicing deli meat, teaching dance, and bartending. He argued that young people should consider what they can demonstrate through a job rather than judging it only by its title or industry.“Even though your life mission isn’t to be the manager of a McDonald’s or a Dairy Queen or whatever, the fact that you can show a future employer that you moved up the line…that’s what you need,” he said.Cuban has worked a shift at Dairy Queen, while Bezos worked at McDonald’s as a teenager. The examples illustrate his argument that starting somewhere can create opportunities to establish a work record.What young workers should learn firstSpeaking separately to Fortune, Cuban said early jobs can teach employees to follow a schedule, work under a manager and cooperate with colleagues from different backgrounds. He highlighted “learning to work for a boss and doing a great job” alongside “learning how to reduce the stress of your boss”.Beyond interpersonal skills, Cuban encouraged workers to understand how their employer makes money, identify opportunities to contribute and learn what progression requires.“Trying to figure out how to become more productive at your job,” he added. Cuban said a substantial career improvement can take two or three years. He acknowledged that workers may feel stuck, but urged them to recognise that frustration without letting it determine their next steps.Other technology leaders stress learning from early workGoogle CEO Sundar Pichai has similarly argued that many early career decisions carry less lasting weight than young people expect.“I’m going to let you in on a little secret: While these things matter in the moment, they are much less consequential than you might think,” he told Stanford graduates.Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, whose early work included washing dishes and cleaning bathrooms at Denny’s, has emphasised resilience.“People with very high expectations have very low resilience—and unfortunately, resilience matters in success,” Huang told students at Stanford.You use AI every day. articles.title: Warsaw-Modlin airport reopens after bomb threat alert on London flight led to temporary closure
articles.summary: A flight from London made an emergency landing at Warsaw-Modlin Airport on Tuesday over fears of an explosive device on board.
articles.body: A flight from London made an emergency landing at Warsaw-Modlin Airport on Tuesday over fears of an explosive device on board. The aircraft, carrying 181 passengers, landed at 10.01am local time after being diverted from its original destination, Warsaw Chopin Airport.The airport was temporarily closed while authorities waited for bomb disposal experts to arrive. Modlin Airport spokesman Adam Szabłowski was reported by GB News stating: “A plane from London landed at Modlin Airport at 10:01am. There are 181 people on board. The airport has been closed. We are waiting for bomb disposal experts.”The airport had earlier said the aircraft landed safely and that security services were verifying the reported threat. It said the bomb alert concerned a flight from London Heathrow to Warsaw Chopin Airport.The incident comes after a separate bomb threat yesterday forced a Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton to Sofia to divert to Budapest on Monday. Hungarian Gripen fighter jets escorted the Airbus A321neo to Budapest, where it landed safely at around 12.09pm local time.Wizz Air said security checks on the aircraft and passengers had been completed and nothing suspicious was found. The airline said it was cooperating with authorities and that the aircraft was expected to resume its journey.Hungarian defence minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said the country’s air-defence alert system had issued an alert after the bomb threat was reported. A Gripen fighter jet took off within minutes and escorted the aircraft to Budapest before returning to its base. Police took charge of the incident after the landing.You use AI every day. articles.title: Fact check: Did N3on accidentally leak Bohemian Grove activities during a livestream?
articles.summary: The viral claim gained traction after a clip showed N3on at an event, with social media users suggesting that he had exposed a secret activity involving
articles.body: The viral claim gained traction after a clip showed N3on at an event, with social media users suggesting that he had exposed a secret activity involving Bohemian Grove members. One post claimed: "N3on IMMEDIATELY Ends Stream after Accidentally Leaking What The Bohemian Grove Members were Doing At his Part Infront of 50k Viewers." The wording sparked curiosity, but the available footage and reporting do not establish that any secret gathering was exposed. Instead, the incident appears to have been linked to a Halloween party hosted by N3on and professional boxer Ryan Garcia.N3on's Bohemian Grove leak claim faces questions over Halloween livestreamThe timeline offers an important clue. N3on and Ryan Garcia hosted a private Halloween party in Los Angeles on October 29, 2026. The event attracted influencers and online personalities, with N3on broadcasting the gathering on Kick.According to Fightnews, the hosts kept the venue details private and shared invitations directly with guests. The party also had restrictions on outside livestreaming because of sponsorship agreements.The event made headlines for a separate confrontation involving streamer Kanel Joseph. Ryan Garcia reportedly asked Joseph to stop recording. When the camera remained on, Garcia slapped it to the ground and also struck Joseph's security guard. TMZ reported that the incident was captured on a livestream.These details establish that filming restrictions were a real issue at the party. However, they do not prove that N3on accidentally revealed anything connected to Bohemian Grove.What is Bohemian Grove, and did N3on expose its members?Bohemian Grove is a private retreat in Monte Rio, California, associated with the Bohemian Club. Its membership has included influential figures from business, politics and other fields. The organisation attracts public interest because of its private gatherings and unusual traditions.One of its best-known events is the Cremation of Care ceremony. Participants perform a theatrical ritual in front of a large owl statue, using an effigy to symbolise the removal of worldly concerns. Footage of the ceremony has circulated publicly for years and has fuelled various conspiracy theories.However, no credible evidence currently connects N3on's Halloween livestream to this ceremony or an actual Bohemian Grove gathering.The viral post also does not establish that the streamer ended his broadcast because of an accidental disclosure. His Kick stream history lists a 3-hour, 43-minute broadcast titled "N3on x Ryan Garcia Halloween Party IRL" on October 29.N3on did livestream a Halloween party with Ryan Garcia, but the claim that he exposed Bohemian Grove activities remains unsupported. The viral caption turns an intriguing clip into a much bigger allegation than the available evidence can justify.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger’s October charity night raised a record $9.75 million for After-School All-Stars, which provides free programmes for nearly 150,000 students across the United States
articles.summary: A single evening of fundraising can make a difference in the lives of thousands of children, particularly when it helps provide access to education,
articles.body: A single evening of fundraising can make a difference in the lives of thousands of children, particularly when it helps provide access to education, mentorship and opportunities beyond the classroom. Actor and former California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger’s annual charity event in Los Angeles has achieved a new milestone, raising a record $9.75 million to support young people across the United States. The money will benefit After-School All-Stars, a non-profit organisation that works with children and young people through free after-school programmes.The Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative reported the record-breaking fundraising achievement in an October 14, 2026, update, noting that the annual Arnold Schwarzenegger–Westime Charity Night brought together supporters for a cause close to the actor’s heart. After-School All-Stars also confirmed the achievement in an October 22 post on its official website, describing the event as its 13th annual charity night. The organisation said the funds would support its nationwide programmes, which serve nearly 150,000 students.Arnold Schwarzenegger’s annual charity event raises $9.75 millionThe 13th Annual Arnold Schwarzenegger-Westime Charity Night was held earlier in October at Schwarzenegger’s home in Los Angeles. The event was co-hosted by Schwarzenegger and John Simonian, founder of luxury watch retailer Westime and a board member of After-School All-Stars. The fundraiser has developed into an important annual gathering for supporters of the organisation. What began as an effort to bring friends and supporters together has grown into a major fundraising occasion, with contributions directed towards programmes for children and young people.This year's total of $9.75 million marks a record for the event. According to After-School All-Stars, the amount represents an investment in the futures of nearly 150,000 students who benefit from its programmes across the country. The organisation emphasised that the fundraising achievement was not simply about collecting a large sum of money. It was about sustaining opportunities for students to discover their interests, develop confidence and work towards their personal and educational goals.What happened during the 13th annual charity night?The evening brought together supporters, entertainers, artists and contributors for a Western-themed celebration. The programme featured several performances and activities, giving guests an opportunity to participate in the fundraising effort while supporting the organisation's work. According to After-School All-Stars' account of the event, the entertainment included line dancing and performances by the two-time Grammy Award-winning Mariachi Divas. Young mariachi performer Mateo Lopez also presented a rendition of the US national anthem, while blues music brought the evening to a close.Guests were offered additional experiences, including customised Western hats, bolo ties and traditional tintype portraits. The event also featured a live auction, with individuals, artists and business partners contributing special items and experiences to help raise funds. Milan Carter served as the evening's emcee, while Chuck Dukas led the auction. Contributors included Richard Mille, MANSORY, boxer Ryan Garcia, Billy Lucas and Daniel Marshall. Artists Nick Moss, Lotte Zhang, Wes Lang and Hiro Yamagata also donated original works of art. The dining arrangements were provided by Wolfgang Puck Catering, with chefs Eric Klein and Garry Larduinat and their team overseeing the food. TOMA also returned to serve its signature empanadas.How After-School All-Stars supports studentsCo-founded by Schwarzenegger more than three decades ago, After-School All-Stars focuses on helping children succeed academically and develop skills that can support them beyond school. Its programmes provide free after-school and summer learning opportunities to students across the United States. The organisation operates at more than 750 schools and community sites nationwide. Its work includes academic support, enrichment activities, opportunities to build friendships and access to caring adults who can guide and encourage young people.These programmes are particularly important because learning and personal development do not stop when the regular school day ends. After-school activities can give children additional time to explore subjects, discover interests and develop abilities that may not receive as much attention during classroom lessons. By keeping programmes free, After-School All-Stars also aims to make these opportunities accessible to children and families who might otherwise face financial barriers to participation.In its October 22 announcement, the organisation highlighted the importance of relationships between students and programme staff. CEO Ben Paul explained that children often remember the people who made a difference in their lives more than individual activities. He emphasised that supportive relationships are central to the organisation's mission of helping young people succeed in school and life.Schwarzenegger's long-standing commitment to the organisationSchwarzenegger's involvement in After-School All-Stars is closely connected to the organisation's founding and its continued efforts to expand opportunities for young people. Through the annual charity night, he has helped bring together donors and supporters to provide financial backing for its work. The latest fundraiser also reflects the role that private contributions and community support can play in sustaining non-profit programmes. While the $9.75 million raised represents a significant achievement, the organisation's work continues throughout the year at schools and community locations across the country.The Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative also highlighted the enthusiasm and generosity of those attending the event. Its director, Monika Langthaler, was present at the gathering and witnessed the support shown for the cause. With its latest fundraising record, the Arnold Schwarzenegger-Westime Charity Night has provided fresh support for an organisation working to make after-school education and enrichment opportunities available to nearly 150,000 students nationwide.You use AI every day. articles.title: Gujarat horror: 2 farm labourers burnt alive inside vehicle over Rs 30,000 dispute
articles.summary: RAJKOT: Two farm labourers, including a 16-year-old boy, were burnt alive after two men set a pick up van on fire on the outskirts of Gundaran village in
articles.body: RAJKOT: Two farm labourers, including a 16-year-old boy, were burnt alive after two men set a pick up van on fire on the outskirts of Gundaran village in Liliya taluka of Amreli district early on Tuesday.The police have arrested two men, including the alleged main accused, in connection with the double murder, which is suspected to have stemmed from a monetary dispute over the purchase of the vehicle.The deceased were identified as Ravi Badhel (16) and Nitin Pachaya (21). Both were natives of Madhya Pradesh and had been working as farm labourers in Gundaran village.The police recovered their half burnt body from the charred vehicle.According to the police, the duo was sleeping inside the vehicle parked at a farm when the accused allegedly arrived during the night, poured petrol on it and set it ablaze.Trapped inside, the two occupants were burnt to death.After learning about the incident, family members, including Ravi's father Kamlesh Badhel, rushed to the spot and tried to douse the flames.However, by the time they could reach the vehicle, both the occupants had died. The Liliya police, along with forensic experts, subsequently reached the scene and launched a probe into the incident.The police registered an offence under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and other relevant provisions. Within hours, they detained the alleged main accused, Vinod Dodiyar, and his relative, Raju Dodiyar.Deputy superintendent of police, Vismay Manseta, said that the murder is suspected to be a fallout of a dispute involving the purchase of the vehicle and an outstanding payment of Rs 30,000.According to the preliminary investigation, Vinod had purchased the passenger vehicle from a man named Riteshsinh on instalments.Although he had already paid a partial amount, Rs 30,000 remained outstanding.Following the payment dispute, Riteshsinh allegedly handed over possession of the vehicle to his friend Kamlesh, the father of one of the deceased.Riteshsinh had reportedly told Kamlesh that he was also owed money by Vinod and would settle the amount with him once Vinod cleared the outstanding dues. He had promised to hand over the vehicle thereafter.However, Vinod allegedly became furious over the vehicle being kept in Kamlesh's possession.When he approached Riteshsinh demanding either the return of the vehicle or a refund of the money he had paid, Riteshsinh reportedly refused both demands.Police suspect that this dispute prompted Vinod and his relative to target the vehicle, unaware or allegedly indifferent to the fact that two people were sleeping inside it."As part of the alleged premeditated plan, the accused first filled petrol in their motorcycle at a fuel station some distance from the crime scene.They then stopped near the farm, transferred petrol from the motorcycle's tank into four to five small cans and allegedly sprinkled it inside and outside the Toofan vehicle before setting it on fire. They subsequently fled from the spot." said police.Ravi's father, Kamlesh, said the vehicle had remained in their possession because of the money owed by Riteshsinh.The police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the double murder and the financial transactions between the parties.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Rajkot | Silver Rate in Rajkot | Bank Holidays in Rajkot | Public Holidays in Rajkot | Rajkot AQI | Weather in Rajkot | Petrol Price in Rajkot | Diesel Price in Rajkot | CNG Price in Rajkot | LPG Price in RajkotStay updated with the latest Rajkot news. articles.title: 'Radical thinking': INDIA bloc allies snub Left leader Neha Bora's 'Brahmanvaad' remark
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress's key ally, Samajwadi Party, has unequivocally distanced itself from the \"Brahmanvaad\" remark of Left-wing student leader Neha Bora.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress's key ally, Samajwadi Party, has unequivocally distanced itself from the "Brahmanvaad" remark of Left-wing student leader Neha Bora.The AISA president, under the patronage of INDIA bloc leaders, gained limelight for fiercely criticising the poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar and the electoral roll purge under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).On Bora's "need freedom from Brahmanvaad" remark, Samajwadi Party's Rajeev Rai said: "Making such a sweeping statement is not appropriate. Every religion has both good and bad people; we shouldn't make such generalisations... We should avoid them. That is exactly what the BJP wants; why should we fall into their trap?"Rai, who represents the Ghosi Lok Sabha constituency in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, firmly repudiated the AISA leader's rhetoric riddled with "sweeping generalisations"."In this day and age, the kind of rhetoric being used is simply unacceptable. There is no basis for it. We shouldn't make sweeping generalisations about any caste, community, religion, or region," he said.Akhilesh Yadav's party is not the only one to shrug off Bora's statement, as Uddhav Sena leader Priyanka Chaturvedi also called her assertions "unfortunate", saying radical thinking, be it from the Right or the Left, is harmful to the nation."It is highly unfortunate. While I believe this may be an old video, it reveals a mindset that asserts rapes happen in temples, are committed by priests, and that Brahmin women are unsafe. I generally avoid focusing on caste, but as a Brahmin woman myself, I must ask: is it appropriate to use such derogatory language? I have always maintained that this kind of radical thinking—whether from the Left or the Right—is harmful to the nation," the former Rajya Sabha member said.She, however, said she would like to "sit down with Neha Bora and explain that not everything should be viewed through the lens of caste or religion"."She is young, talented, bright, and smart, with the drive to fight for a cause; she ought to use her intellect more constructively," Chaturvedi said.Earlier, the BJP targeted Bora over a video showing her criticising the “Brahmanical system”, with party spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accusing her of spreading “Hindu hate”.Sharing the video on X, Bhandari called Bora the “poster girl” of what he described as Rahul Gandhi’s anti-Hindu politics.In the video, Bora is heard speaking about women's safety and criticising the Brahmanical system. She reportedly referred to the Unnao and Kathua cases while making her remarks.Bhandari also linked her comments to an earlier statement by Rahul Gandhi on the safety of women."Neha Bora poster girl of Rahul Gandhi displays her Hindu hate," Bhandari wrote.He added, "She is inspired from Rahul Gandhi who earlier had said 'Mandiro main ladkiyon ke sath ched chad hoti hai'.""Congress Hates Hindus, loves vote bank! Congress Soch is a threat to India's unity!" Bhandari posted.The remarks triggered a political row after the video surfaced on social media. However, the clip is undated, and the circumstances in which Bora made the comments could not be independently verified.Bora has been actively involved in protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.She took part in an October 10 demonstration organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student groups in Delhi. Police detained several protesters, including Bora, as restrictions on public gatherings were imposed in parts of the capital.The AISA president also backed the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally against the CEC, urging people to join the opposition's demonstration in Delhi.She has also appeared alongside Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders during protests against the poll body chief. Bora was also present at "mock" Parliament which was organised to symbolically "impeach" Gyanesh Kumar.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
