articles.body: TOI Correspondent From Washington: Donald Trump made an unlikely political breakthrough in 2024, prising away a slice of Indian-American voters from a community that had reliably backed Democrats for decades. Two years later, the romance appears to have soured.A new survey by the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace finds that the Republican gains have largely evaporated, with Indian-Americans swinging back towards Democrats ahead of the November 2026 midterms. According to the Indian American Attitudes Survey conducted in October, 62 per cent of Ind-Am citizens intend to vote Democratic in their congressional district, against just 19 per cent backing Republicans, whittled down from nearly 30 per cent who voted for Trump in 2024. Another 12 per cent are undecided. In 2024, Kamala Harris retained 62 per cent support, but Trump improved his showing to 30 per cent. Democratic support subsequently slipped to 57 per cent in January 2026 before recovering to 62 per cent, still short of the years they leaned heavily Democratic but a distinct uptick.The community's return to traditional Democratic preference appears to reflect its immigrant and minority experience, support for legal immigration and social welfare, and discomfort with the MAGA Republican Party's association with Christian evangelicalism and perceived intolerance of minorities.Previously, their economic success, entrepreneurship, lower-tax preferences and concerns about illegal immigration made some desis receptive to Republican arguments. Trump's cultivation of PM Modi, including their high-profile Howdy Modi rally in Houston in 2019, also improved his standing.The subsequent Trump second term presidency, however, has exposed the limits of that appeal. Immigration crackdown, including efforts to restrict birthright citizenship and the hex on H1B visas and workplace raids have struck particularly close to home in a community with extensive family and professional connections to India. After the University of Texas football team defeated Ohio State, French posted a photograph of brown students celebrating in the stands, suggesting their presence illustrated how Americans had been displaced by foreigners. The implication that students who looked Indian were somehow not American provoked outrage, inviting criticism from moderate Republicans like Senator John Cornyn, who has been sidelined by Trump, who has made little effort to contain the rampant racism of his nativist MAGA flock.Yet the Democratic resurgence is not necessarily an ideological conversion, with 35 per cent of those intending to vote Democratic say opposition to Republicans, rather than enthusiasm for Dems, is their primary motivation. Meanwhile, 26 per cent identify as independents, underscoring the community's political fluidity.With more than 5.2 million people of Indian origin, roughly 1.5 per cent of the US population, Indian-Americans cannot determine a national election by themselves. But their concentration in California, New Jersey, Texas, Georgia, Michigan, Illinois and the Washington metropolitan area gives them influence in closely contested races.The message for Republicans clearly is that economic conservatism and affinity with Modi cannot indefinitely outweigh anxieties about immigration and belonging. For Democrats, the lesson is not to take the community's support for granted. The 2024 Republican breakthrough showed that Indian-American voters are persuadable. The 2026 survey suggests they are now heading back to the Dem fortress.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Debra clashes expose BJP’s factional feud; MLA discharged
articles.summary: Debra BJP MLA Subhashis Om alleges assault in party clash over molestation complaint and extortion claims; rival leader denies, cites CCTV; police complaint pending.
articles.body: Debra (West Midnapore): Discharged from a private hospital in Midnapore town on Tuesday, Debra BJP MLA Subhashis Om renewed allegations that a rival party faction assaulted him during Monday’s street clashes. Tension remained high in the area as the MLA traded sharp counterclaims with Ghatal organisational district president Tanmoy Das.The legislator alleged he was attacked at the 10/2 Dua anchal office on Monday while trying to stop an internal brawl. “A woman in Dua region was going to lodge a molestation complaint against party workers. While we reasoned with her against reporting colleagues, a section of workers turned violent, tried to loot and assaulted me,” Om said.Party sources, however, said Monday’s violence erupted at the anchal office after a woman party functionary was allegedly molested and assaulted. When she set out for Debra police station to file a complaint, Om and his supporters allegedly intercepted her and other workers — blocking them again near the police station — to dissuade them from reporting colleagues. Sources traced the feud to alleged multi-lakh-rupee extortion surrounding the “Ravan Pora” event and resentment over awarding Balichak Utsav tenders to Jharkhand and Odisha traders.Das rejected the assault claim, accusing Om of staging a drama after walking into the hospital normally and putting on bandages only upon spotting media. “No one laid a finger on the MLA. CCTV footage retrieved by police from the anchal office, police station and hospital premises will clear everything,” Das said, adding that the assaulted woman functionary was stopped from reaching the police station and the hospital. Das promised internal action if any worker attacked the lawmaker.Reacting to the conflict in Kharagpur on Tuesday, senior minister Dilip Ghosh said, “If there has been any dispute among ourselves, the party will look into it. And if an incident of violence or a clash has occurred, police will take action according to law. If it is an internal matter, the party will certainly inquire into it,” Ghosh said.Both Om and Das have sent reports to state party bosses. articles.title: Kailashpati Mishra’s birth anniversary to be observed as state function: BJP
articles.summary: BJP pays tribute to Kailashpati Mishra in Buxar; Sanjay Saraogi says his birth anniversary will be a state function from 2027; library planned in his memory.
articles.body: Patna: The BJP on Tuesday paid tribute to veteran party functionary and former minister Kailashpati Mishra on his death anniversary at his native Barka Dhakaich village in Buxar, where state party president Sanjay Saraogi announced that his birth anniversary would be observed as an official state function from 2027. The education department also announced to build a library in his memory in Buxar.At the memorial meeting, Union minister of state for home Nityanand Rai and agriculture minister Vijay Kumar Sinha were among those present, along with several NDA functionaries, legislators and BJP workers.Rai described Mishra as a leader who carved out a distinct identity through his ideas, discipline and dedication to the organisation. Saraogi said Mishra, a founding member of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh and BJP, played a significant role in expanding the party’s organisational network in Bihar and nurturing generations of workers.Saraogi said the decision to observe Mishra’s birth anniversary as a state function had received cabinet approval. He also assured the Kailashpati Mishra Smriti Parishad that efforts would be made to fulfil its demands, including the installation of a life-sized statue.For the proposed library, education department secretary Rajiv Roshan has written to the Buxar DM to identify suitable land on the premises of SP Vidya Mandir School in Civil Lines and submit details of its area, ownership, boundaries and present status, along with a no-objection report.Education minister Mithilesh Tiwari said the library would have physical and digital facilities, including biographies of Mishra and other eminent personalities and a collection of his poems. articles.title: Coimbatore corporation to introduce biweekly e-waste collection drives
articles.summary: COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation plans to introduce biweekly e-waste collection drives in all 100 wards by partnering with a private
articles.body: COIMBATORE: The Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation plans to introduce biweekly e-waste collection drives in all 100 wards by partnering with a private recycling company. The civic body is in the process of signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with an authorised e-waste processing firm to ensure scientific disposal and recycling of discarded electronic appliances.The move follows a month-long collection campaign conducted between Oct 2 and 31 under the Centre’s Special Campaign 6.0, during which the corporation collected 21,467kg (21.46 tonnes) of e-waste from its five zones.Dedicated collection points were established to encourage residents to hand over discarded electronic and electrical equipment separately. The corporation organised awareness rallies, camps, exhibitions, kolam competitions and two-wheeler rallies involving school students, self-help groups and residents.Green Era Recyclers, which contributed to the collection and processing initiative, received a certificate of appreciation from corporation commissioner Katta Ravi Teja on Oct 31.The commissioner said the proposed drives would provide residents with a regular channel to dispose of obsolete electronic goods, including computers, mobile phones and household appliances, instead of mixing them with regular garbage or allowing them to enter informal recycling channels.He said, “The initiative is expected to strengthen the city’s waste segregation system under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, which came into force on April 1. According to the new rule, e-waste has been separately categorised. The same company that processed during the pilot collection will continue once the MoU is signed. articles.title: Pocso accused held for murder attempt on survivor jumps from court building
articles.summary: Pocso accused Mohammed Adinan arrested for stabbing 14-year-old survivor in Perumbavoor; later jumped from court building, treated for minor injuries, remanded.
articles.body: Kochi: A 22-year-old Pocso case accused, who allegedly attempted to kill the survivor in the case while out on bail, attempted to harm himself by jumping off the first floor of a court complex in Perumbavoor on Tuesday afternoon.Perumbavoor Police arrested Mohammed Adinan of Arakkapady on Monday for assaulting the 14-year-old survivor. The police said Adinan allegedly trespassed into the house where the survivor lives, assaulted her and stabbed her. A neighbour, who intervened after hearing her screams, was also injured in the attack.As residents rushed to the spot, the attacker escaped and hid in bushes in the area. The police later arrested Adinan with the help of residents. The accused allegedly resisted arrest, but he was overpowered and taken into custody. The police said he allegedly attacked her for filing the complaint and sending him to jail.The police had arrested Adinan in the first week of Aug and remanded in judicial custody for sexually assaulting the girl. He was released on bail by the end of Oct.Meanwhile, Adinan, who received minor injuries after jumping from the building, was given medical attention before being shifted to prison. articles.title: HC seeks details of all captive elephants in Keralam
articles.summary: Kerala High Court orders district collectors to compile details of all captive elephants via village officers within 2 weeks; report to be filed by Dec 4.
articles.body: Kochi: The high court on Tuesday directed all district collectors in the state to collect details of every captive elephant in their respective jurisdictions through village officers within two weeks.The district collectors shall submit the details collected to the chief wildlife warden within one week thereafter. The chief wildlife warden shall compile the information and place the report before the court within a further week, a bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji ordered. The court was considering petitions alleging gross abuse, torture and mismanagement of captive elephants.The bench directed that the information collected should include the name of each elephant, its registration number, if registered, the owner’s name, details of the ownership certificate, the name of the person in possession of the elephant and any other identifying details, including the presence of an embedded microchip and its registration number. The court clarified that the directions would apply to all captive elephants, whether owned by devaswoms, other religious institutions or private individuals. It adjourned the petitions to Dec 4.During the hearing, the court observed that the need to maintain captive elephants with dignity and kindness stemmed not merely from constitutional or statutory prescriptions but also from inherent humanism. “A community that does not take care of its captive animals can never be called civilised, and no amount of excuses can justify actions to the contrary,” the bench observed. The court further said it was the responsibility of the system to ensure that captive animals were treated with care and compassion, and that this responsibility could not be left to individual citizens to lodge complaints or pursue litigation. “The endeavour of this court is to get control over the situation by ensuring that the statutory requirements are implicitly met. But before that, it certainly requires a full list of all captive elephants in Kerala, whether they are registered or otherwise,” the bench observed.It further noted that the list maintained by the wildlife department might not be up to date and that the court could not wait for it to be updated. Accordingly, it directed the district collectors to obtain the details of captive elephants through village officers in their respective jurisdictions.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news.
